neet_che_u05_t01_1.working: Vapour pressure is an intensive equilibrium property. It depends only on the nature of the liquid and the temperature, not on the amount of liquid or the container size.

neet_che_u05_t01_4.working: A: p_A = p_A^0 x_A (II). B: y_A = p_A/p_total (IV). C: p_total = p_A^0 + (p_B^0 - p_A^0)x_B (III). D: 1/p_total = y_A/p_A^0 + y_B/p_B^0 (I).

neet_che_u05_t01_5.working: A is true: a non-volatile solute lowers the solvent's vapour pressure. B is false: vapour pressure does not depend on the amount of liquid. C is true: the vapour is richer in the more volatile component. D is true: Raoult's law is the special case of Henry's law with K_H = p^0.
